title: Add conservative hedged retries and compat wrappers for polyglot SDK bridge
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Several production customers saw tail latency amplification in bursty workloads when transient infra blips caused single-request retries to back off for the full retry window. Hedged (speculative) retrying can reduce p99/p999 by issuing a conservative duplicate request after a short, tunable window. This PR introduces a transport-agnostic hedged-retry abstraction and lightweight compatibility wrappers across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDK facades so teams can opt into hedged policies without changing higher-level call sites.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds hedged-retry policy abstraction in the core SDK bridge with a conservative default (hedge after 75ms for generation calls, configurable per-route).
- Provides thin compat wrappers for Python, TypeScript and Go SDKs (opt-in flag: hedged=true) that preserve existing retry semantics when disabled.
- Includes telemetry and two new metrics: hedged_request_count and hedged_failover_latency_ms (histogram). These are emitted at the SDK bridge and forwarded to the existing telemetry pipeline.
- Adds lightweight unit/integration tests and e2e experiment harness used to validate p99 improvements under noisy-worker scenarios.
- Bumps minor versions: python sdk -> 2.3.0, typescript sdk -> 1.12.0, go sdk -> v1.9.0 (packaging + changelogs added).

Compatibility and safety:
- The hedged behavior is opt-in at the SDK call-level and opt-out globally via environment variable REDWOOD_SDK_HEDGE=off. Default remains conservative and disabled for blocking (non-stream) legacy endpoints, enabled by default for streaming/generation optimized calls in the polyglot test harness.
- No breaking changes to public API shapes; wrappers translate hedged calls to existing call signatures.
- Added guardrails: concurrent-hedges-per-route limit, a max-duplicate-quota to avoid cost blowouts, and backpressure-aware cancelation of the slower duplicate when the first response completes.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests added for hedged policy scheduling, cancelation semantics, and telemetry emission (py/ts/go).
- Integration tests use the perf-canary harness to simulate noisy worker nodes (script: scripts/hedge_canary.sh).
- E2E experiment reported: 27% median p999 reduction and 9% p99 reduction on a synthetic bursty generator workload (details in docs/perf/hedged_retry_eval.md).

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind hedged flag for initial rollout. Start with internal canary apps and two early customers. Monitor hedged_request_count/cost_ratio and hedged_failover_latency_ms for 48h before enabling broader rollout.

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus on transport-agnostic API (core/hedge.go, core/hedge.py, core/hedge.ts) and the cancelation semantics between duplicate requests.
- Telemetry naming chosen to match existing SDK metrics conventions; if we want a different prefix please call it out.

Checklist:
- [x] Core hedged abstraction and scheduler implemented
- [x] Python/TypeScript/Go thin wrappers added and unit-tested
- [x] Telemetry and histograms wired to the pipeline
- [x] Changelogs and packaging bumps included
- [x] Docs and perf writeup added

Migration/Maintenance:
- Developers should prefer the hedged compat wrapper on new generation/low-latency streaming routes. The default can be toggled via env or per-call options. Expect to monitor cost-to-latency tradeoffs; added an alert recipe in observability-pack to watch hedged cost ratio.

References: Linear ENG-4281, internal playbook: docs/ops/hedged_retry_playbook.md, and perf notes at docs/perf/hedged_retry_eval.md.
